logline: Two young boxers team up with a moneylender to bring down a predatory loan shark syndicate, trading economic desperation for kinetic hand-to-hand combat in modern Seoul.

bollymeter.basis: 89 percent Rotten Tomatoes from 9 critics, 91 percent audience Popcornmeter, and IMDb 8.1 converge on the same read: exceptional fight choreography and a charismatic bromance carry a narrative that critics found exciting rather than complex.

pull_quotes.text: The entertaining rapport and sympathetic dynamic between its two leads make audiences root for their success.
The chemistry between actors and tasty moral dilemmas push Bloodhounds to the next level.
It's exciting instead of complex and visceral instead of emotional.

seasons.review_body: Adapted from a Naver webtoon by Jeong Chan, Season 1 dropped June 9, 2023 on Netflix and earned a place in TIME's 10 Best Korean Dramas of 2023. The 89-percent Rotten Tomatoes score from 9 critics pointed to one engine: the physical performances of Woo Do-hwan and Lee Sang-yi, whose boxer chemistry and hard-contact fight choreography set the show apart from corporate-thriller peers. Ready Steady Cut's caveat - 'exciting instead of complex' - captured the honest ceiling: the show is not interested in moral nuance, only in escalating the stakes and keeping the bromance warm. Lee Sang-yi won the Excellence Award at the 2023 Korea Drama Awards. The 91-percent Popcornmeter and IMDb 8.1 confirm the audience loved exactly what it promised.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the show's core proposition efficiently: Gun-woo and Woo-jin meet in a boxing match, their complementary styles hinting at the partnership ahead. The loan-shark economy is drawn quickly and without sentimentality, giving the action stakes a credible material base.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The boxing ring meeting between Gun-woo and Woo-jin - the bromance that anchors the entire series introduced in a single bout.

critic_note.text: Bloodhounds delivers some great action sequences. It is bloody, it is gory, and it is definitely impactful.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 8
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The season finale escalates to a full-scale siege with the action choreography the show built its reputation on. The resolution is cathartic within the show's own populist terms and set up the season 2 expansion with clarity.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The extended warehouse fight sequence - the show putting every frame of its choreography budget on screen.

critic_note.text: This K-drama also has a brutal take on morality alongside sweet bromance elements.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 arrived April 3, 2026, shifting the arena from Seoul loan-shark networks to an international underground boxing league. Rain joins as the new antagonist Baek-jeong, while Woo Do-hwan and Lee Sang-yi return. At the time of writing, critical aggregation is still forming and no verified scores are available. The expansion to a global criminal network is a significant tonal shift from the domestic class-war intensity of season 1.
seasons.season_over_season: Moves from street-level Seoul debt violence to an international boxing syndicate; Rain's addition as villain raises the star wattage but the jury is out on whether the scale upgrade retains the bromance warmth that drove season 1.
